feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so no result is stated for it. Iteration 1 (0.12 m track, score 482.7) is the best evidence: oval 20/20, s-bend 5/20, slalom 0/20, with failures all off-track at max_error 0.060 to 0.064 m and rms_error 0.023 to 0.030 m. Iteration 3 (0.10 m track only, score 357.3) fell to s-bend 1/20 and oval 14/20, and iteration 2 (0.10 m plus span, mass and lead changes, score 411.7) also fell. So the limit is bend excursion, and narrowing the track has moved it the wrong way. This package widens the track to 0.14 m with everything else as in iteration 1, including kp 1.6, so the track effect is isolated.

Answers to your integration questions, from evidence so far: (1) Signal linearity and sensor saturation cannot be separated yet, because the 0.06 m span was never changed alone. (2) Oscillation at 0.10 m was 0.291 to 0.299 on the oval, close to the 0.12 m value, so the narrower track did not add much jitter. (3) Control effort on the s-bend was 5.9 at 0.12 m and 4.98 at 0.10 m, which suggests the narrower track demanded less steering effort per bend. (4) Peak max_error is on bends, with line loss at the same bends (slalom 1.0 event per run on both tracks), so the peak location is not yet resolved. (5) Signal weights: the outer sensors carry the largest weights, and no evidence yet shows they are over-driving the signal.

Next race: if s-bend completions rise above 5/20 and max_error stays under 0.06 m on more runs, keep wheel_track at 0.14 m and try 0.16 m, which tests whether the trend continues. If the score falls below 482.7 with slalom line_loss_events rising, the wider track is too slow for the slalom, so return to 0.12 m and move to a sensing change. If the oval steering_oscillation falls and the s-bend does not improve, the track is not the limit, so keep 0.12 m and change the sensor geometry alone.
requested_changes: If s-bend completion rises above 5/20 and max_error falls below 0.06 m on more runs: try wheel_track 0.16 m, keeping all other fields the same. Evidence: 0.10 m (iteration 3) gave s-bend 1/20 and 0.12 m (iteration 1) gave 5/20, so the trend is monotonic over that range.

If slalom line_loss_events rise above 1.0 per run while the s-bend does not improve: return wheel_track to 0.12 m and change sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 m only. Evidence: iteration 1 slalom was 1.0 line-loss event per run with max_error 0.064 m, and the 12 mm footprint has not yet been tested with the 0.12 m track and 7-sensor span.

If the wider track is clean on the s-bend but the score still sits near 482.7, try the sensor span at 0.10 m (x = -0.05, -0.0333, -0.0167, 0, 0.0167, 0.0333, 0.05) with wheel_track 0.14 m. Evidence: iteration 2 widened the span to 0.15 m together with a narrower track and mass change, and its s-bend fell to 0/20, so a narrower span is the less risky direction to test.
